DataComR

Source: GLOSSARY.md

An R package that compares two datasets the way SAS PROC COMPARE does, giving users familiar with PROC COMPARE a similar tool in R.

Datasets and matching

Base dataset: The dataset treated as the reference in a comparison; differences are reported relative to it. Avoid: Reference, source, left, df1, expected

Compare dataset: The dataset checked against the Base dataset. Avoid: Target, right, df2, actual

Observation: One row of a dataset. Avoid: Row, record

Variable: One column of a dataset, identified by its exact, case-sensitive name. Avoid: Column, field, feature

ID variable: A variable whose values together identify which Base observation pairs with which Compare observation. Avoid: Key, join column, by variable

Matched observation: A Base observation and a Compare observation paired by their ID values, or by position when there are no ID variables.

Unmatched observation: An observation present in only one of the two datasets. Avoid: Orphan, extra row, missing row

Duplicate ID: A set of ID values shared by more than one observation within the same dataset; such observations are reported but never paired or compared. Avoid: Duplicate key, non-unique row

Variables

Common variable: A variable present in both datasets.

Type family: The SAS-like kind a variable belongs to — numeric, character, date or datetime — which decides whether two variables’ values can be compared at all.

Conflicting types: A common variable whose Base and Compare versions belong to different type families, so its values are not compared.

Attribute difference: A mismatch in a common variable’s label, SAS format or width, reported separately from value differences.

Values

Comparison method: The rule deciding whether two numeric values are equal: exact, absolute, relative or percent. Avoid: Tolerance mode

Criterion: The threshold a comparison method tests the difference against. Avoid: Tolerance, epsilon

Unequal value: A matched observation where a common variable’s Base and Compare values are not equal under the comparison method. Two missing values are equal; a missing value against a non-missing value is unequal; special missings are equal only when they carry the same letter; character values differing only in trailing blanks are equal. Avoid: Mismatch, diff, discrepancy

Results

Listing: The printed, PROC COMPARE-style report of a comparison. Avoid: Report, output

Return code: A single integer whose bits flag each kind of difference found, laid out as SAS’s SYSINFO. Avoid: Status, exit code
